messages:
Sam: taking over night shift — handing off an active alert stream. root issue: KV cache evictions in eu-west-1 started ~00:58 UTC, spike in embeddings tail latency and ~502s for a subset of requests. Pager fired for Priya earlier; i'm primary now. brief summary: cache nodes hitting memory pressure -> eviction thrash -> cache miss storm -> upstream model hosts see queued tokens -> elevated latency + errors. customers affected: 2 high-usage tenants (tracking CUST-421, CUST-422).
ops-bot: [ALERT] kv-cache-eu-west1.evictions > 150/min (group: infra-kv) — triggered at 00:58 UTC — severity: P1 (auto-page)
Priya: quick notes from initial response — bumped `maxmemory` on the hot shard group and temporarily increased eviction threshold. ran a rolling restart on the worst offenders (shard-7, shard-9). saw evictions drop ~40% after restart but latency still elevated. leaving the restart in place. ✅
Sam: actions in flight (do not re-run without confirming):
- added extra `maxmemory` to the hot group via `kubectl patch` (see command below)
- enabling prefaulting on warm pool to absorb bursts
- starting a small traffic reroute to warm-serving pool for embeddings route `embed.v1.large` (canary)
- opened customer tickets and notified CSMs (Ava)
Priya: command snippets I used:
```
# patch mem limit for cache statefulset
kubectl patch sts kv-cache-hot -n infra --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/resources/limits/memory","value":"12Gi"}]'
# quick redis check
redis-cli -h shard-7.info PING
redis-cli -h shard-7.info INFO memory | egrep "used_memory_human|maxmemory"
```
Jon: saw the canary reroute go to warm pool — traffic 5% shifted, error rate for canary down to baseline. note: warm pool instances are smaller; sustained reroute will increase cost and may increase latency for other customers. if evictions continue after 30m, propose failover of the worst shard group to dedicated capacity (requires ops manager signoff).
Ava: CSM update: CUST-421 reports timeouts in their embedding batch jobs (started 01:05 UTC). They are in a production rollout, asked for ETA. told them we're mitigating and will provide hourly updates. CUST-422 is larger but lower QPS; they saw retries — created internal ticket. Customers asked about SLA exposure.
Sam: runbook references:
- runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-eviction
- playbook excerpt: increase mem -> rolling restart -> prefault warm pool -> reroute -> failover to dedicated
- escalation: if >20% error-rate for 30m -> page infra-lead and oncall-manager
Priya: current metrics snapshot post-restart + reroute:
- evictions/min (eu-west1): 62 (was 180)
- embeddings 95p latency: 720ms (baseline 220ms)
- errors (502/504) across embedding route: 1.8% (baseline 0.05%)
- canary error rate: 0.1%
Sam: coverage: i'm primary for the next 4h. Priya is sec until 01:40 UTC then Jon will take secondary coverage through the night. Ava is handling customer comms. gap: no on-call with deep storage/redis expertise after 03:00 UTC — pinging @infra-lead to confirm late-night backup.
Jon: note about rollback attempt — i tried to revert one minor config change from earlier deploy but it was a red herring. deploy-bot shows no model-serving deploys at 00:50-01:10 UTC. copying logs here:
```
deploy-bot: deploys: []
# tail from cache logs
[01:02:12] shard-9: used_memory_human: 9.8G maxmemory: 10G
[01:02:45] shard-9: evicted_keys: 412
[01:03:10] shard-7: evicted_keys: 488
```
ops-bot: [UPDATE] kv-cache-eu-west1.evictions dropped below threshold at 01:20 UTC (auto-clear pending)
Sam: current mitigation status:
- increased memory limits: done (Priya)
- rolling restarts: done (Priya)
- canary reroute -> warm pool: in progress (Jon) — 5% traffic
- prefault warm pool: in progress
- customer comms: in progress (Ava)
- escalation if not resolved in 60m: planned
Priya: open TODOs for incoming shift: verify lasting stability for 60m, keep canary at 5% and monitor p95 and errors, do not increase canary >10% without approval. if evictions climb back >120/min rollback the mem change and prepare failover plan.
Sam: handoff checklist for next oncall (Jon covers next):
1) confirm evictions stay <80/min for 60m
2) keep canary at 5% and watch canary_error_rate <0.5%
3) if embeddings p95 >500ms for 30m -> escalate to infra-lead and prepare dedicated failover (cost impact noted)
4) keep customers informed hourly
Jon: acknowledged, i'll take over at 01:40 UTC and will start with a health-check script: `scripts/health_check_eu_west.sh` (runs cache, router, and embeddings smoke tests).
Ava: i'll send a 01:40 UTC update to CUST-421/422 and attach current mitigation summary.
Sam: wrapping up — leaving this thread as the canonical handoff. ping me if anything spikes. i'll escalate to oncall-manager in 60m if not back to baseline. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: [NOTE] This thread archived to incident log 2026-07-11-KV-eviction (internal).
